title: Spark Savings defines a take rate limit and then sets it to unlimited on every live vault
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.5.2.1.4 defines the control precisely: "The take rate limit defines the maximum amount **and pace** of withdrawals from a Spark Savings vault permitted by the taker role." The taker role (.1.3) can "withdraw a Spark Savings vault's underlying asset from the vault to the Spark Liquidity Layer ALM Proxy contract."

Every live configuration in A.6.1.1.1.3.5.2.2 records `Take rate limit: unlimited` — USDC on Ethereum (2 billion supply cap), USDT on Ethereum (4 billion), ETH on Ethereum, USDC on Avalanche (500 million), PYUSD on Ethereum (250 million), USDG on Robinhood Chain (500 million), USDT on Arbitrum (250 million). Seven vaults, seven unlimited.

So nothing throttles the movement of user deposits out of these vaults. Whatever the taker key can sign, it can move at once and in full.

The rest of the design shows this is a deliberate allocation of trust rather than an oversight. The three roles are separated across distinct addresses; the default admin — controlling upgrades and overall vault authority — is assigned to Spark governance "to ensure maximum possible security and decentralization" (.1.1); the setter is bounded on both sides by min and max yield (.1.5, .1.6). Protection is placed in *who holds the keys* and in the supply cap bounding total exposure, not in a velocity limit on withdrawal.

That is a coherent position, and it is also the exact inverse of how the Spark Liquidity Layer treats its own conduits, where `maxAmount` and `slope` throttle every direction. The same organization applies a rate limit to capital it sends into third-party protocols and declines to apply one to user deposits leaving its own vaults — and the vaults are where the larger, less sophisticated balances sit.
description: The parameter is specified to cap the amount and pace of taker withdrawals, yet all seven configured vaults — including 4 billion USDT and 2 billion USDC supply caps — record it as unlimited.
